Summary of Cookie Auth - POST /api/snwebrtc/webrtccookieauth/cookieauth

This API endpoint provides a short-lived ticket that the WebRTC phone widget uses to connect to the ServiceNow voice service and initiate calls. It allows guest users to place calls without requiring login credentials. The endpoint is accessible via a POST request to/api/snwebrtc/webrtccookieauth/cookieauth.

Show full answer Show less

Access Control and Trusted Domains

The endpoint only issues tickets if the orchestratorhost matches a trusted domain or its subdomain. Trusted domains are configured in the system property snwebrtc.orchestrator.trusteddomains, which by default includes sncapps.service-now.com. Only users with the maint role can modify this property.

Request Parameters and Headers

  • Request Body (JSON):
    • voiceserviceid (required): The 32-character sysid of the voice service configuration, must be lowercase hexadecimal.
    • orchestratorhost (required): The hostname or HTTPS URL of the voice orchestrator; must match a trusted domain and cannot include ports, paths, queries, or credentials. HTTP URLs are rejected.
    • instancename (required): The ServiceNow instance identifier (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, max 63 characters).
  • Headers:
    • Accept: Specifies response format (default is application/json).
    • Content-Type: Must be application/json, otherwise request is rejected with status 400.
    • X-UserToken: Required session CSRF token for security; requests missing or having incorrect tokens are rejected.

Response and Status Codes

  • On success (HTTP 200), the response body contains a single-use, 60-second expiration wsticket string for WebSocket connection to the voice orchestrator.
  • Common error responses:
    • 400 Bad Request: Invalid parameters, incorrect content type, untrusted orchestrator host, or oversized request body. The error message is generic due to security considerations.
    • 502 Bad Gateway: The instance failed to obtain a ticket from the voice orchestrator.

Practical Use

ServiceNow customers integrating WebRTC voice capabilities can use this endpoint to securely obtain a temporary ticket needed for the WebRTC phone widget to establish voice calls without user login. Ensuring the orchestrator host is trusted and providing correct request parameters and headers are essential for successful ticket generation.

The included cURL example demonstrates how to call this API with JSON data and required headers, which can be adapted for your instance and orchestrator details.

URL format

Default URL: /api/sn_webrtc/webrtc_cookie_auth/cookie_auth

Trusted orchestrator domains

The Cookie Auth POST endpoint creates a ticket only when the orchestrator_host value matches a domain in the following system property, or is a subdomain of one of those domains. If the property is empty, the endpoint uses the default domain, sncapps.service-now.com.

Property Description Default value
sn_webrtc.orchestrator.trusted_domains Comma-separated list of trusted domains. A host is trusted when it equals one of the domains or is a subdomain of one of them. Only users with the maint role can change this property.

Data type: String

cURL request

The following example demonstrates how to use the POST endpoint to request a ticket for a voice service. The request includes the session CSRF token header.

curl "https://instance.service-now.com/api/sn_webrtc/webrtc_cookie_auth/cookie_auth" \
        --request POST \
        --header "Accept: application/json" \
        --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
        --header "X-UserToken: session_csrf_token" \
        --data "{\"voice_service_id\": \"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\", \"orchestrator_host\": \"https://myservicenoworchestrator.sncapps.service-now.com\"}"

Response body. The response contains the ticket.

{
        "ws_ticket": "ticket_value"
